transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-01-30 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya/ Daniel/ Lina (Redwood) — Priya/ Tom/ Samir (Kestrel)

Summary:
Quick renewal + expansion check-in. Kestrel wants to extend current Dedicated commitment for another 12 months, add APAC region with burst capacity, and formalize a staging-onprem pilot for sensitive PHI requests. Main concerns: predictable latency p95, cost per 1k tokens at heavy ingest, SOC 2 attestation window and KMS integration. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send a detailed provisioning matrix with sample traffic patterns and cost scenarios; SE to run targeted perf benchmarks; procurement to align on PO timing.

Topics covered:
- Current utilization and forecasted uplift by product team (triage & triage+ chatbots)
- APAC region activation and cold-start concerns
- Private on-prem pilot for PHI-sensitive subset (data residency / KMS)
- Pricing tiers, burst policy, SLA targets and remediation windows
- Legal / procurement dependencies and timeline

Action items (recorded here and in metadata):
- See metadata action_items for owners/dates

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining on a Friday, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Priya (Kestrel): Hi all, Priya here — head of platform. Tom and Samir on.
[00:00:10] Tom (Kestrel): Tom, SRE lead.
[00:00:12] Samir (Kestrel): Samir — procurement.
[00:00:15] Daniel (Redwood SE): Daniel here. I'll be covering the provisioning matrix and perf notes.
[00:00:20] Maya: High level, we heard you're looking to renew the Dedicated commitment and add APAC region and a private pilot for some PHI flows, is that right Priya?
[00:00:29] Priya: Yep, that's it. We have a few production signals — our triage bot traffic will double during influenza season and we want the safety net to avoid throttling. Also we need APAC because latency for our Sydney customers is spiking to 280–350 ms on P95 today.
[00:00:45] Daniel: Got it. For Dedicated we typically recommend sizing based on 95th percentile token throughput per minute and then adding a 30% burst buffer. We can show examples in the matrix.
[00:00:56] Tom: Curious about cold starts when we spin up APAC nodes. We saw previous cold start hits when we tried region failover in November. Is there warm standby or prefix caching we can use?
[00:01:10] Daniel: Yes, there are a couple of levers. One is pre-warmed pools (reserved instances in APAC) and another is prefix/KV caching — though caching helps only when prompts share prefixes. For SLOs you can combine pre-warm + autoscale policies; latency hit during scale is usually under 200ms extra for our Llama-family and Mistral-ish models but it depends on sequence length. (note: transcription sometimes shows "Mizzral").
[00:01:36] Priya: Sequence length for our triage flow is average 280 tokens, peaks 1.2k for long histories. Any quantization or batch tuning recommendations here?
[00:01:45] Daniel: For long context we can move to a quantized variant to reduce GPU memory pressure; however p95 latency can increase if you over-quantize. Our recommendation: 8-bit quant for background scoring, full-precision for low-latency chat paths. We'll call this out per-model in the matrix.
[00:01:59] Maya: On pricing, we previously discussed committed throughput discounts. Samir, what procurement cadence do you need?
[00:02:05] Samir: We need final pricing by Feb 3 so legal can start redlines; PO ideally signed by Feb 17. Can Redwood provide a 1-page amortized cost table that maps committed units to monthly invoices?
[00:02:16] Maya: Yes — we'll include an amortization view in the provisioning matrix.
[00:02:19] Lina (CSM): Also we'll show a burst usage example — how billing works when you exceed reserved capacity and how failover to Hosted tier would be priced.
[00:02:27] Tom: About the private pilot — we need to ensure KMS integration with our existing HSM via Azure Key Vault and that audit logs are forwarded to our Splunk cluster. Is that supported in the Private offering or do we need an onprem instance?
[00:02:42] Daniel: Both are possible. Private VPC with KMS integration is supported; for strict PHI and air-gapped needs we recommend on-prem deployment. For audit logs we can stream to your Splunk using our audit webhook; we'll include sample schemas. Note: some events may be batched which affects near-real-time log shipping.
[00:03:01] Priya: SOC2 evidence — we need our vendor SOC2 report and encryption key rotation cadence. What's Redwood's current attestation?
[00:03:09] Maya: We're SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certified; we'll share the cert package and our key rotation policy. Lina will attach the security pack.
[00:03:17] Samir: Anything else on the compliance front that could delay PO? We may have to run a short security questionnaire.
[00:03:22] Lina: We can fill your standard vendor questionnaire and offer a controlled instance for penetration testing after the PO.
[00:03:28] Tom: Can we talk expected p95 numbers for APAC on a pre-warm + 2x autoscale config? Ballpark?
[00:03:34] Daniel: Ballpark p95 for chat-style (avg 280 tokens) with pre-warm + 2x autoscale on Nvidia A10-like infra is ~110–150ms. For longer contexts up to 400–500ms. We'll put model-specific p95 ranges in the matrix.
[00:03:49] Priya: We need a stress scenario in the doc — like 2x sustained for 6 hours and a 10x minute-level spike.
[00:03:56] Daniel: We'll add those workloads and show cost and latency impacts. We'll also include a suggested autoscale policy: steady-state target 70% GPU utilization, scale step of 25% every 60s, with a max burst pool.
[00:04:11] Maya: On contractual terms — are you looking to keep the same term length?
[00:04:14] Priya: Prefer 12 months but open to 18 if the price break is meaningful. Also need a clause for adding APAC after a 60-day lead time.
[00:04:24] Samir: And a clause for rollback to current geography in the event of missed SLA.
[00:04:28] Maya: We can do SLA credits for missed p95 windows and a rollback clause tied to incident thresholds. Legal can draft sample language.
[00:04:36] Tom: One practical thing — when we flip to APAC, what are the DNS / routing requirements? Do we need to update firewall rules or can Redwood's edge handle region routing?
[00:04:45] Daniel: Redwood's smart routing can direct requests by region header or IP. For Private deployments you'll need to open specific egress ports for the control plane; we'll provide a minimal firewall rule set.
[00:04:55] Priya: Great. For benchmarking, can Redwood run tests against our near-prod dataset? We'll scrub PHI but keep token-length distribution.
[00:05:03] Daniel: Yes, we can run a bench if you provide a scrubbed dataset and a runbook. We'll need a 72-hour window and a contact for quota bump.
[00:05:12] Samir: On billing: how are burst invoices itemized? We want to ensure we can map charges back to product teams.
[00:05:19] Lina: We'll provide per-route usage breakdowns and token-level cost export. We can also create tags for product-team level allocation.
[00:05:27] Priya: Any blockers on our side before legal and procurement can proceed?
[00:05:30] Maya: Only the provisioning matrix + pricing sheet and the SOC2 docs. We'll send both by Feb 3.
[00:05:36] Samir: Perfect. If we get that by Feb 3 we should be on track to PO by Feb 17.
[00:05:41] Priya: Let's also schedule the benchmarking week — week of Feb 8 works for our infra team.
[00:05:45] Daniel: I'll follow up with suggested windows and the perf checklist.
[00:05:50] Maya: Quick recap — Redwood will: (1) send provisioning matrix + amortized pricing + burst examples + security pack by Feb 3, (2) SE will coordinate benchmark runs week of Feb 8, (3) procurement will confirm PO timeline by Feb 10. Any other dependencies?
[00:06:04] Tom: We'll verify network egress rules and provide scrubbed dataset.
[00:06:08] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:06:11] Maya: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with the doc links.

(Transcription notes: occasional speaker overlap, some product names transcribed imperfectly — e.g., "Mistral" as "Mizzral", "KV cache" as "kay vee cash").

Shared resources referenced during call:

End of transcript.
